ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $CD$ is the altitude of $ \triangle ABC$, $AE$ is the angle bisector of $ \triangle ABC$, and $CD$ intersects $AE$ at point $G$. Given $\angle BCD = 50^\circ$ and $\angle BEA = 110^\circ$, find the measure of $\angle ACD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By the given information, $CD$ is the height of $\triangle ABC$,\\
hence $\angle BDC=\angle ADC=90^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle B=90^\circ-\angle BCD=90^\circ-50^\circ=40^\circ$.\\
In $\triangle ABE$, $\angle BAE=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle BEA=180^\circ-40^\circ-110^\circ=30^\circ$.\\
Since $AE$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAC=2\angle BAE=60^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle ACD=90^\circ-\angle BAC=\boxed{30^\circ}$.

Since $AE$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$,\\

Therefore, $\angle ACD=90^\circ-\angle BAC=\boxed{30^\circ}$.
